numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For a sparse subtype that cannot hold NA (Sparse[int64, nan]), cumprod and cummin return 0 where the dense result has NaN, so NA gaps are accumulated as real values; cumsum(skipna=False) also gives non-NaN values after the gaps; a RuntimeWarning 'invalid value encountered in cast' leaks.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Results should match the dense computation: NA gaps stay NaN and propagate as in the dense result, with no leaked RuntimeWarning. Dense reference values are [1.0, nan, 5.0, nan] for cumprod, [1.0, nan, 1.0, nan] for cummin, and [1.0, nan, nan, nan] for cumsum(skipna=False).
trigger_conditions: SparseArray subtype cannot hold NA, e.g. Sparse[int64, nan], Sparse[uint8, nan], or Sparse[bool, nan]
operation is cumprod, cummin, or cummax (accumulation through _accumulate)
cumsum with skipna=False (the numeric fast path that returns early is skipped when skipna is False)
cumsum with skipna=True is not affected because the numeric fast path returns before densifying
_accumulate densifies with to_dense(), which casts the fill value NaN into the integer/bool subtype

input_output_examples.input: arr = pd.arrays.SparseArray([1.0, np.nan, 5.0, np.nan]).astype(pd.SparseDtype("int64", np.nan)); ser = pd.Series(arr); list(ser.cumprod())

numerical_characteristics.dtype: Sparse[int64, nan] (passages also cite Sparse[uint8, nan] and Sparse[bool, nan]); result dtype Sparse[float64, nan], or Sparse[object, nan] for bool cumprod/cummin/cummax
category_specific_evidence: NaN is the special value involved: the gaps of a Sparse[int64, nan] (or uint8/bool subtype) are NA, not 0.

Entry point: SparseArray._accumulate densified with to_dense(), which is np.asarray(self, dtype=self.sp_values.dtype) and casts the NaN fill value into the subtype, so gaps reach na_accum_func as 0/False.
Correct handling: use _densify(), which promotes an NA fill value with maybe_promote instead of casting it into the subtype; the gaps then stay NaN.

Reproducer with arr = SparseArray([1.0, nan, 5.0, nan]).astype(SparseDtype('int64', nan)): cumprod gives [1, 0, 0, 0] (dense [1.0, nan, 5.0, nan]); cummin gives [1, 0, 0, 0] (dense [1.0, nan, 1.0, nan]); cumsum(skipna=False) gives [1, 1, 6, 6] (dense [1.0, nan, nan, nan]).
A leaked RuntimeWarning 'invalid value encountered in cast' accompanies the wrong results.
cumsum(skipna=True) escapes the bug because the numeric fast path returns before densifying; the 'and skipna' gate is why skipna=False is affected.
Expected subtype after fix: int64 only for cumsum with skipna=True; float64 otherwise; object for the bool-subtype cumprod/cummin/cummax case.
